theorem_title: Height comparison at a strict divisor-degree ratio
natural_language_statement:
Shinichi Mochizuki, *Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position*, February 2009.

Theorem 2.1(i) — printed page 11 / PDF page 11:

> Write $\omega_X$ for the canonical sheaf on $X$. Suppose that $U_X$ is a hyperbolic curve — i.e., that the degree of the line bundle $\omega_X(D)$ is positive.

Theorem 2.1(ii), opening clauses — printed page 11 / PDF page 11:

> Let $P \overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}$ be the projective line over $\mathbb{Q}$; $C \subseteq P$ the divisor consisting of the three points “0”, “1”, and “$\infty$”;

A selected opening clause; the original sentence continues with further data.

Proof of Theorem 2.1 — printed page 12 / PDF page 12:

> Now set $E \overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \phi^{-1}(C)_{\mathrm{red}} \subseteq X$ [so $\phi^*\omega_P(C) \cong \omega_X(E)$].

Proposition 1.4(i) — printed page 6 / PDF page 6:

> (i) We have
> $$
> \operatorname{ht}_{\overline{\mathcal{L}}\otimes\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(x)=\operatorname{ht}_{\overline{\mathcal{L}}}(x)+\operatorname{ht}_{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(x)
> $$
> for $x \in X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$.

Proposition 1.4(iii) — printed page 6 / PDF page 6:

> (iii) The BD-class of $\operatorname{ht}_{\overline{\mathcal{L}}}$ depends only on the isomorphism class of the line bundle $\mathcal{L}_{\mathbb{Q}}$ on $X_{\mathbb{Q}}$. In particular, it makes sense to write $[\operatorname{ht}_{\mathcal{L}}]$ or $[\operatorname{ht}_{\mathcal{L}_{\mathbb{Q}}}]$ for the BD-class $[\operatorname{ht}_{\overline{\mathcal{L}}}]$ of $\operatorname{ht}_{\overline{\mathcal{L}}}$.

Definition 1.2(ii), opening segment — printed page 5 / PDF page 5:

> (ii) Fix a subset $\mathcal{F} \subseteq X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$. If $\alpha,\beta : \mathcal{F} \to \mathbb{R}$ are functions, then we shall write
> $$
> \alpha \lesssim_{\mathcal{F}} \beta\quad (\text{respectively, }\alpha \gtrsim_{\mathcal{F}} \beta;\ \alpha \approx_{\mathcal{F}} \beta)
> $$
> if there exists a [“constant”] $C \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\beta(x)-\alpha(x)\leq C$ (respectively, $\alpha(x)-\beta(x)\leq C;\ |\alpha(x)-\beta(x)|\leq C$) for all $x \in \mathcal{F}$;

Opening segment ends at the original semicolon. The order of the two one-sided inequalities is transcribed as printed; the two-sided absolute-value condition is the relevant one here.

Proof of Theorem 2.1, lead-in and first line of displayed calculation — printed page 13 / PDF page 13:

> Thus, by Proposition 1.4, (i), (iii), we compute to find that
> $$
> \operatorname{ht}_{\omega_X}\ \approx\ \operatorname{ht}_{\omega_X(E)}-\operatorname{ht}_E\ \approx\ \operatorname{ht}_{\omega_P(C)}-\operatorname{ht}_E
> $$

Only the first line of the displayed calculation is selected. The display continues with inequalities. The source uses the height on P along the map phi in this calculation; no pullback/composition symbol has been inserted into the quotation.

These passages supply the original-paper parent context: the three-cusp divisor C, the log-canonical pullback isomorphism for the reduced inverse-image divisor E, additive heights, invariance of height BD-classes under line-bundle isomorphism, and the resulting height decomposition in the proof of Theorem 2.1. The exact auxiliary identity canonical+cusp = polar(phi)+div(r), with an explicit rational-function witness r, is a statement to be proved in the formal Genl/Heights/Belyi source; it is not quoted verbatim from this paper. Likewise, a uniform bound for arbitrary explicit polar presentations from a principal relation requires the precise quantifiers, presentation data, and constants established by the formal source. The paper states the parent relation using line bundles and BD-classes; it does not state those two auxiliary lemmas in their explicit presentation-level form.

GenEll directly supplies the required parent context. Definition 1.5 defines reduced divisors, log-different, and log-conductor; it is not a source of an explicit polar-presentation height decomposition. Noncritical Belyi Maps Theorem 2.5 is the existence premise for the map cited in GenEll; no additional quotation from it is needed for these height/divisor nodes.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.divisorDegreeHeightComparison`

Let $N$ be a natural number and let $F$ be an intermediate field between $\mathbb Q$ and an algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q(T)$, with elements $u,v$ such that $u$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, $u^N+v^N=1$, $F=\mathbb Q(u,v)$, and $F$ is finite-dimensional of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb Q(u)$. A place $P$ means a valuation subring $O_P\ne F$ containing every rational number; write $k_P$ for its residue field. Assume every $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring and every $k_P$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$. For $f\in F$, put $o_P(f)=-\log_0(V_P(f))$, where $V_P$ is the valuation on $F$ from the maximal ideal of $O_P$ and $\log_0$ is the integer-valued total logarithm called `WithZero.log` in the code, and put $m_P(f)=\max(0,-o_P(f))$. A point $x$ consists of such a place $P_x$ and a ring homomorphism $\sigma_x:k_{P_x}\to\overline{\mathbb Q}$; for $f\in O_{P_x}$ write $f(x)=\sigma_x(\bar f)$, put $L_x=\sigma_x(k_{P_x})$ and $d_x=[L_x:\mathbb Q]$. For an algebraic number $z$, write $h(z)=\operatorname{logHeight}_1(z\text{ viewed in }\mathbb Q(z))/\deg(\mu_z)$, where $\mu_z$ is its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb Q$. Set $H_f(x)=h(f(x))$ if $f\in O_{P_x}$ and $H_f(x)=0$ otherwise. A presentation $R=(f,g)$ of a divisor $B$ means $B(P)=m_P(f)-m_P(g)$ at every place, and its height is $h_R(x)=H_f(x)-H_g(x)$; zero functions and common poles are not excluded. For every pair of finite-support integer-valued functions $D,E$ on the places, every presentation $R_D$ of $D$, every presentation $R_E$ of $E$, and every real $q$, if $\deg D=\sum_P D(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]>0$ and $\deg E=\sum_P E(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]<q\deg D$, then there exists $C\in\mathbb R$ such that $h_{R_E}(x)\le qh_{R_D}(x)+C$ for every point $x$. The degree inequality is strict; no sign assumption on $q$, no effectiveness assumption on $D,E$, no restriction to affine points, and no pole-avoidance condition is present, so the stipulated zero heights at poles remain part of the conclusion.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.divisorDegreeHeightComparison`

设 $N$ 为自然数，$F$ 为 $\mathbb Q$ 与 $\mathbb Q(T)$ 的一个代数闭包之间的中间域，且有元素 $u,v$ 满足：$u$ 在 $\mathbb Q$ 上超越，$u^N+v^N=1$，$F=\mathbb Q(u,v)$，并且 $F$ 在 $\mathbb Q(u)$ 上有限维且维数为 $N$。这里的位 $P$ 是包含所有有理数且不等于 $F$ 的赋值子环 $O_P$，其剩余域记为 $k_P$。假设每个 $O_P$ 都是离散赋值环，每个 $k_P$ 在 $\mathbb Q$ 上都有限维。对 $f\in F$，令 $o_P(f)=-\log_0(V_P(f))$，其中 $V_P$ 是由 $O_P$ 的极大理想给出的 $F$ 上的赋值，$\log_0$ 是代码中名为 `WithZero.log` 的取整数值的全定义对数；再令 $m_P(f)=\max(0,-o_P(f))$。点 $x$ 由这样的位 $P_x$ 及环同态 $\sigma_x:k_{P_x}\to\overline{\mathbb Q}$ 组成；当 $f\in O_{P_x}$ 时，记 $f(x)=\sigma_x(\bar f)$，并令 $L_x=\sigma_x(k_{P_x})$、$d_x=[L_x:\mathbb Q]$。对代数数 $z$，记 $h(z)=\operatorname{logHeight}_1(z\text{ 视为 }\mathbb Q(z)\text{ 中的元素})/\deg(\mu_z)$，其中 $\mu_z$ 是 $z$ 在 $\mathbb Q$ 上的最小多项式。若 $f\in O_{P_x}$，令 $H_f(x)=h(f(x))$；否则令 $H_f(x)=0$。除子 $B$ 的表示 $R=(f,g)$ 是指对每个位都有 $B(P)=m_P(f)-m_P(g)$，其高度定义为 $h_R(x)=H_f(x)-H_g(x)$；并未排除零函数或共同的极点。对这些位上每对具有有限支撑的整数值函数 $D,E$、$D$ 的每个表示 $R_D$、$E$ 的每个表示 $R_E$ 以及每个实数 $q$，若 $\deg D=\sum_P D(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]>0$ 且 $\deg E=\sum_P E(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]<q\deg D$，则存在 $C\in\mathbb R$，使每个点 $x$ 都满足 $h_{R_E}(x)\le qh_{R_D}(x)+C$。次数不等式是严格的；没有假设 $q$ 的符号或 $D,E$ 的有效性，没有把点限制为仿射点，也没有避开极点的条件，因此在极点处规定的零高度仍属于结论。

**日本語**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.divisorDegreeHeightComparison`

自然数 $N$ に対し、$F$ を $\mathbb Q$ と $\mathbb Q(T)$ の代数閉包の間の中間体とし、$u,v\in F$ が、$u$ は $\mathbb Q$ 上超越的、$u^N+v^N=1$、$F=\mathbb Q(u,v)$、および $F$ は $\mathbb Q(u)$ 上有限次元でその次元は $N$、という条件を満たすとする。ここで素点 $P$ とは、すべての有理数を含み $F$ と異なる付値部分環 $O_P$ をいい、その剰余体を $k_P$ と書く。すべての $O_P$ が離散付値環であり、すべての $k_P$ が $\mathbb Q$ 上有限次元であると仮定する。$f\in F$ に対し $o_P(f)=-\log_0(V_P(f))$ と置く。ただし $V_P$ は $O_P$ の極大イデアルによる $F$ 上の付値、$\log_0$ はコードで `WithZero.log` と呼ばれる整数値の全域的対数である。また $m_P(f)=\max(0,-o_P(f))$ と置く。点 $x$ は、そのような素点 $P_x$ と環準同型 $\sigma_x:k_{P_x}\to\overline{\mathbb Q}$ の組である。$f\in O_{P_x}$ のとき $f(x)=\sigma_x(\bar f)$ と書き、$L_x=\sigma_x(k_{P_x})$、$d_x=[L_x:\mathbb Q]$ と置く。代数的数 $z$ に対し、$\mathbb Q$ 上の最小多項式を $\mu_z$ とし、$h(z)=\operatorname{logHeight}_1(z\text{ を }\mathbb Q(z)\text{ の元とみなす})/\deg(\mu_z)$ と書く。$f\in O_{P_x}$ のとき $H_f(x)=h(f(x))$、それ以外のとき $H_f(x)=0$ と置く。因子 $B$ の表示 $R=(f,g)$ とは各素点で $B(P)=m_P(f)-m_P(g)$ が成り立つことをいい、その高さを $h_R(x)=H_f(x)-H_g(x)$ とする。零関数や共通の極は排除されていない。素点上の任意の有限台の整数値関数 $D,E$、それぞれの任意の表示 $R_D,R_E$、および任意の実数 $q$ に対し、$\deg D=\sum_P D(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]>0$ かつ $\deg E=\sum_P E(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]<q\deg D$ ならば、実数 $C$ が存在し、すべての点 $x$ で $h_{R_E}(x)\le qh_{R_D}(x)+C$ が成り立つ。次数の不等式は厳密であり、$q$ の符号や $D,E$ の有効性は仮定しない。点をアフィン点に限る条件も極の回避条件もないので、極で零と定義した高さも結論に含まれる。
